A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IF-CRITIC research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; visual inspection resolves interleaved table text from extraction.

before.justification: v1 reports original critic evaluations, component ablations, human assessments of explanations, and DPO/GRPO optimization experiments, including general-benchmark results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports alternative-backbone evaluations and a manual audit of training critiques.

M1.justification: The checklist generator, four-stage critique filtering, SFT and constraint-level DPO procedure, and reward calculation remain unchanged. The alternative-backbone experiments test the existing framework rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same instruction collections, four meta-evaluation datasets, and downstream instruction-following and general benchmarks. Despite shorter table headings in v2, meta-evaluation still uses first-turn Chinese Multi-IF. The added backbone study and quality audits do not introduce different task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces GLM-4-Plus with Gemini-3-Pro under both prompting strategies. GLM-4-Plus remains a critique-verification model, but no longer participates in that comparison. The other general-model, evaluation-specific, and downstream reward-model comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 newly reports evaluations of five alternative critic backbones and a human audit of 70 final critiques covering 353 constraints. It also distinguishes constraint and complete-checklist correctness in the retained 1,000-sample generator assessment. Existing benchmark splits, decoding procedures, and optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E and Table 5 add a bounded sensitivity study of backbone family and size, while Section 3.3 adds direct checking of filtered training-critique quality. The original component ablations, human explanation comparisons, and reward-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies changed seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added quality assessments report correctness proportions rather than new uncertainty estimates, and the reward-curve figures are retained.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Gemini-3-Pro average F1 scores of 0.857 and 0.855 and removes GLM-4-Plus scores of 0.738 and 0.685. Table 5 adds alternative-backbone results. The generator's previously unspecified accuracy above 99% becomes 99.29% constraint correctness and 97.50% complete-checklist correctness; the new critique audit reports 96.03% judgment and 92.35% explanation correctness. Retained benchmark, ablation, optimization, and general-benchmark values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The critique representation, explanation-selection definitions, SFT and DPO objectives, preference-pair construction, and reward formula in Equations 1–6 are mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list now explicitly highlight superiority over Gemini-3-Pro alongside o4-mini, replacing the highlighted Deepseek-R1 comparison. The central contributions concerning fine-grained evaluation, critique filtering, preference optimization, and efficient downstream improvement remain intact.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section explicitly identifies length-only rule verification and possible self-enhancement or verbosity biases. Appendix E interprets the backbone results as supporting approximately 14B parameters as a performance-efficiency compromise. v2 also explains the many explanation-quality ties and qualifies the preference of reasoning models for checklist-level prompting.

D1.justification: The access statement expands from code to code and model availability. v2 discloses annotator background, compensation, informed participation, and harmful-instruction filtering. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit mention of LLM-based quality filtering of optimization seed instructions, without establishing that preprocessing actually changed. Training hyperparameters, hardware, API cost, and prompt templates are otherwise retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to RuleR and Gemini and removes Vicuna and How Far Can Camels Go? along with the discussion of earlier simple-instruction work. Publication updates for works such as IOPO, VerIF, and Direct Judgement Preference Optimization concern existing references. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose, renames the framework section Methodology, numbers sections, and introduces lettered appendices. Response-model and baseline lists move into appendices, and optimization details are consolidated. These edits improve navigation while retaining the original main argument and section sequence.

P2.justification: The manuscript is comprehensively retypeset with different page geometry, typography, heading styles, page footers, and colored references. Table 1 is reordered and highlighted, a new backbone-results table is added, and Figure 3 is restyled and relocated while preserving its percentages. Figures, tables, and appendix material are reflowed throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through the more competitive Gemini comparison, backbone study, and direct training-critique audit, while making incomplete rule coverage and evaluation bias explicit. These additions improve support and transparency despite the loss of GLM-4-Plus comparison rows and one preprocessing disclosure. The net gain is limited because the central method and most empirical evidence were already present in v1.
